**Word or character limit:** [e.g. "max 50 words"]
**Where it appears:** [e.g. "product page under the title", "category listing", "marketplace bullet"]
**Brand voice:** [e.g. "warm and practical", "premium and minimal"]
**Words to avoid:** [e.g. claims we can't make, competitor names]

Rules for every blurb:
- Open with a specific, engaging phrase about what the product does for the buyer, not a generic opener; vary the openings across rows.
- Include that row's keyword once, naturally.
- Use only the facts in that row. If a row lacks enough detail, write [NEEDS DETAIL: what's missing] instead of inventing features.
- Turn features into benefits (e.g. "moisture-wicking" becomes staying dry on long walks).
- No two blurbs may share a sentence or repeat the same structure back to back.
- Stay within the limit; no health, safety, or environmental claims unless the row states them.

Return a table: Row ID | Product name | Blurb | Word count. Then list any rows flagged for missing detail so I can fix them in the sheet.
variables: e.g. "fabric features and benefits", "key specs", "use cases"
e.g. claims we can't make, competitor names

title: Write webinar reminder messages that raise show-up rates
description: A reminder sequence by email and calendar that gets more registrants to actually attend live.
content:
Write a reminder sequence that gets more of my webinar registrants to show up live. This is step 3 of a webinar pack; it works on its own, but paste your registration page or title and promise from earlier steps if you have them.

**Webinar title, date, time, and join link:** [DETAILS]
**Takeaways and anything attendees get only live:** [e.g. live Q&A, a template, a live teardown]
**Registrants so far and when most registered:** [NUMBERS - or "unknown"]
**Channels I can use:** [email, calendar invite, SMS (with consent), LinkedIn event]
**Typical show-up rate for my past webinars:** [% or "first one"]

Return:
1. **Confirmation email** (sent instantly): what they signed up for, add-to-calendar link, one thing to think about before the session, and a question they can reply with to shape the content.
2. **Calendar invite text:** title, join link, and one-line agenda in the description.
3. **Reminder 1** (3-7 days before): a sneak peek of one insight or the live-only element.
4. **Reminder 2** (day before): agenda and what to prepare.
5. **Reminder 3** (1 hour before): short, just the link and the hook.
6. **"We're live" message** (at start time): one line with the link.
7. **Optional SMS versions** under 160 characters - only for people who opted in to texts.

Rules: Each reminder gives a new reason to attend; don't repeat the same text. Keep the join link in every message. Suggest 2 things that improve show-up beyond messages (e.g. a live-only bonus, asking registrants to submit questions).
variables: e.g. live Q&A, a template, a live teardown
email, calendar invite, SMS (with consent), LinkedIn event

title: Audit my recurring meetings and decide which to cut, shorten, or redesign
description: Reviews your whole set of recurring meetings and recommends which to keep, cut, merge, shorten, or move async to win back time.
content:
Audit my recurring meetings and tell me which to keep, cut, merge, shorten, or move to async.

**My role and main priorities this quarter:** [ROLE, 2-3 PRIORITIES]
**My recurring meetings:** [LIST EACH: name, frequency, length, number of attendees, my role (organizer / required / optional), what it is for, what usually happens. A calendar export pasted as text works.]
**Hours per week I want to win back:** [e.g. "4 hours"]
**Meetings I cannot change:** [e.g. "my manager's staff meeting"]

For each meeting, assess:
- Purpose: decision, problem-solving, alignment, relationship, or information sharing.
- Value to my priorities (High / Medium / Low).
- Overlap with other meetings on the list.
- Whether I need to attend, or whether someone else or a written update could cover it.
- Weekly time cost for me and total cost for all attendees.

Return:
1. **Audit table:** | Meeting | Hours/week (me) | Purpose | Value | Recommendation (Keep / Shorten / Reduce frequency / Merge with X / Move async / Delegate / Leave / Cancel) | Reason |
2. **Total hours saved** if I follow the recommendations, against my target.
3. **Redesigns** for the 2-3 meetings worth keeping but fixing: new purpose, length, attendees, and agenda format.
4. **Messages** I can send: one to an organizer to propose a change, one to step out of a meeting politely, and one to my team announcing changes to meetings I own.
5. A simple rule for accepting new recurring invites in future.

Base time figures only on what I provide; do not invent attendance or costs.

title: Build a decision log from several meetings' notes
description: Combines notes from multiple meetings into one running log of decisions, dates, owners, and status so nothing gets relitigated.
content:
Build a decision log from the notes of several meetings so my team has one place to see what has been decided.

**Project or team:** [NAME]
**Meeting notes, labeled with date and meeting name:** [PASTE EACH SET OF NOTES]
**Existing decision log (if any):** [PASTE or "none"]

Rules:
- Only log real decisions: something agreed by the person or group with authority. Proposals, preferences, and "we should probably" go in a separate "Not yet decided" list.
- If a later meeting changed an earlier decision, keep both entries: mark the earlier one "Superseded" and link it to the new one.
- Flag contradictions between meetings that nobody resolved.
- Do not invent owners, dates, or reasons. Use **[NOT STATED]** where the notes are silent.

Return:
1. The decision log as a table I can paste into Excel or a shared doc:
| ID | Date | Meeting | Decision | Decided by | Rationale (short) | Affects | Status (Active / Superseded / Under review) | Related actions |
2. **Not yet decided:** items discussed repeatedly with no decision, and how many meetings they have come up in.
3. **Conflicts to resolve:** decisions that contradict each other or were reversed without explanation.
4. A short note on how to keep this log updated after each meeting (who adds entries, when, and what counts as a decision).

title: Build a meeting agenda that leads to decisions
description: Designs a timed agenda around the outcomes the meeting must produce.
content:
Act as a meeting design expert focused on decision quality and time efficiency.

**Context**
I need to run a [DURATION]-minute meeting with [AUDIENCE] to achieve [OBJECTIVE].

**Task**
Design an agenda that allocates time based on decision importance, not equal time per topic. Identify what should be discussed, decided, deferred, or handled asynchronously. Make the desired outcome for each section explicit.

**Format**
Return a table:
| Time | Topic | Purpose | Decision/Outcome | Owner |
Also provide a one-sentence meeting objective.

**Meeting context:** [PASTE]

title: Combine a week of meeting notes into one action tracker
description: Pulls actions from several meetings into one deduplicated weekly tracker with owners, due dates, status, and overdue flags.
content:
Combine actions from this week's meetings into one tracker I can manage from.

**Meetings, each labeled with date and name:** [PASTE NOTES OR TRANSCRIPTS FOR EACH MEETING]
**Last week's tracker (if any):** [PASTE or "none"]
**Today's date:** [DATE]
**How I will use it:** [Excel / Planner / a shared doc / a Teams or Slack post]

Rules:
- Merge duplicates: the same action raised in two meetings becomes one row, listing both sources.
- Carry over open items from last week's tracker and update their status if any meeting mentioned progress.
- Only record owners and dates that are stated. Use **[NO OWNER]** or **[NO DATE]** otherwise, and list those for me to assign.
- Flag anything past due as of today.
- Do not invent actions from general discussion; if something sounds like an action but nobody committed, put it under "Possible actions to confirm".

Return:
1. **Tracker** (paste-ready table): | ID | Action | Owner | Due | Status (Not started / In progress / Done / Blocked / Overdue) | Source meeting(s) | Notes |
2. **This week's priorities:** the top 5 actions by urgency and impact.
3. **Needs an owner or date.**
4. **Blocked items** and what is blocking them.
5. **Possible actions to confirm.**
6. A 5-line summary I can post to the team in Teams or Slack.
variables: PASTE NOTES OR TRANSCRIPTS FOR EACH MEETING
Excel / Planner / a shared doc / a Teams or Slack post

title: Decide whether this meeting needs to happen or can be handled async
description: Tests a planned or recurring meeting against clear criteria and recommends meet, shorten, go async, or cancel, with the message to send.
content:
Help me decide whether this meeting really needs to happen.

**Meeting purpose as stated in the invite:** [PASTE INVITE OR DESCRIBE]
**Attendees and their roles:** [LIST]
**Length and frequency:** [e.g. "60 min, one-off" / "30 min weekly"]
**What happened last time (if recurring):** [BRIEF NOTES]
**My role:** [organizer / attendee / my manager's meeting]

Test it against these questions:
- Is there a decision to make, a problem to solve together, or a relationship to build? Or is it mainly sharing information?
- Does it need real-time back-and-forth, or could people respond in writing?
- Does every attendee need to be there, or only for part of it?
- Is the needed input or pre-work ready, or will the meeting stall?
- What is the cost in people-hours (attendees x length x frequency)? Use only the numbers I gave; do not invent salaries or rates.
- What breaks if it does not happen?

Return:
1. **Recommendation:** Meet as planned / Meet but shorter or with fewer people / Replace with an async update / Cancel. Give a one-line reason.
2. A one-line answer to each question above, showing how it pushed the recommendation.
3. If it should still happen: a tighter purpose statement, the right attendee list, and the right length.
4. If not: what to do instead (e.g. email, Teams or Slack thread, shared doc with comments, a 10-minute call between two people).
5. A short, polite message I can send to the organizer or attendees proposing the change. If I am not the organizer, keep it suggestive, not presumptuous.

title: Define the decision a meeting must make and what to read beforehand
description: Pins down the one decision a meeting exists to make, the options, and a short pre-read so people arrive ready to decide.
content:
Help me define exactly what decision this meeting needs to make, and what participants should read before they arrive.

**Meeting topic and attendees:** [TOPIC, NAMES AND ROLES]
**Who has the authority to decide:** [PERSON OR GROUP]
**Background material available:** [PASTE OR LIST DOCUMENTS, DATA, EMAILS]
**Deadline that makes this decision urgent:** [DATE OR EVENT]

Steps:
1. Write the decision as a single question that can be answered at the meeting (e.g. "Do we launch in Q3 with reduced scope, or delay to Q4 with full scope?"). If the topic is too broad for one decision, split it and tell me which part must be decided first.
2. List the realistic options, including "do nothing" or "decide later" where relevant.
3. List the criteria the decision should be judged on, and any constraints (budget, policy, deadlines).
4. Identify what each attendee must know beforehand to decide well.

Return:
1. **Decision question** (one sentence) and **decision owner**.
2. **Options** with a one-line summary of each.
3. **Decision criteria.**
4. **Pre-read:** a note under 400 words covering context, options, key facts, and the question, plus a list of the specific documents or sections to read (with page or section names), marked Must read / Optional.
5. **Agenda line** to put in the invite (e.g. "Decide: X. Please read the pre-read by Tuesday 5 pm.").

Do not add facts or figures that are not in my material; mark gaps as [CONFIRM].
variables: PASTE OR LIST DOCUMENTS, DATA, EMAILS

title: Design a leadership team offsite that ends in real decisions
description: An offsite agenda with pre-work, sessions, facilitation notes, and a decision log so the time produces outcomes.
content:
Help me design an offsite for my leadership team.

**Team:** [NUMBER of people and roles]
**Length and setting:** [e.g. "1.5 days, in person"]
**Why now:** [e.g. "annual planning", "team isn't aligned on strategy", "new leaders joined"]
**Decisions we must leave with:** [SPECIFIC decisions]
**Tensions or unspoken issues:** [e.g. "sales and product disagree on roadmap", "trust is low between two leaders"]
**Facilitator:** [me / a leader / external]

Design:
1. Pre-work: what each person prepares and reads, due a week before, so no time is spent presenting status.
2. Agenda: sessions with time, goal, format (discussion, exercise, decision), and the output each session produces. Balance hard business decisions with time on how we work together.
3. Facilitation notes for the two hardest sessions: opening questions, how to surface disagreement, and how to close on a decision.
4. Decision method: how we'll decide when we don't agree (who has the final call, and "disagree and commit").
5. A decision and action log template: Decision | Owner | Deadline | How we'll communicate it.
6. Follow-through: what gets shared with the company and when, and the 30-day check-in.

If I'm both CEO and facilitator, warn me where that will suppress candor and suggest ways around it.

title: Draft a public meeting agenda and minutes that meet open meetings law
description: A compliant public body agenda with specific item descriptions and action-focused minutes that record motions and votes accurately.
content:
Help me prepare the agenda and minutes for a public body meeting.

**Public body:** [e.g. "city council", "planning commission", "advisory board"]
**Meeting type:** [regular / special / closed or executive session portion]
**Open meetings law that applies:** [e.g. "state open meetings act"; paste posting and minutes requirements if available]
**Agenda items:** [LIST with what action is expected on each]
**Closed session items, if any:** [topic and the legal basis we expect to rely on]
**For minutes, my notes or transcript:** [PASTE, including motions, movers, seconders, and votes]

Part 1: Agenda
- Standard order: call to order, roll call and quorum, approval of agenda, public comment, consent items, action items, reports, adjournment.
- Describe each item specifically enough that a member of the public knows what may be decided (not "Old business" or "Discussion"). Mark each as action or information.
- Include public comment instructions, remote participation details, and an accommodation statement.
- For closed session items, give a description of the topic and a placeholder for the legal basis: [CONFIRM AUTHORITY WITH COUNSEL].

Part 2: Minutes
- Action minutes, not a transcript: attendance, quorum, each item with a short summary, the exact motion, mover and seconder, and the vote by name (yes, no, abstain, absent).
- Record recusals and stated conflicts of interest.
- Summarize public comments neutrally by speaker name and topic, as our practice requires.
- Do not characterize members' motives or add commentary.

Rules: never invent votes, motions, or attendance; mark anything unclear in my notes [CONFIRM]. Remind me to check posting deadlines with our clerk.
variables: regular / special / closed or executive session portion
LIST with what action is expected on each
topic and the legal basis we expect to rely on
PASTE, including motions, movers, seconders, and votes

title: Facilitate a fair performance calibration meeting
description: Prepares an agenda, ground rules, bias checks, and facilitator prompts to run a calibration session that produces consistent ratings.
content:
Help me facilitate a performance calibration meeting with a group of managers.

**Group being calibrated:** [team/function, number of employees, levels]
**Rating scale and definitions:** [PASTE]
**Target or guideline distribution (if any):** [e.g. none / guidance only]
**Pre-submitted ratings summary:** [counts by rating per manager - optional]
**Time available:** [e.g. 2 hours]
**Known challenges:** [e.g. one manager rates everyone high, new managers, remote vs. office employees]

Give me:
1. **Pre-work for managers** - what to bring for each person (evidence of results and behaviors against level expectations, not adjectives).
2. **Agenda with timings** - prioritize discussion time on borderline cases and top/bottom ratings rather than reviewing everyone equally.
3. **Ground rules** - confidentiality, evidence over impressions, compare to the level standard not to each other, everyone speaks.
4. **Bias checks to call out live** - recency, halo/horns, proximity (remote vs. in office), leniency/severity by manager, similarity, and patterns by gender, race, or leave status.
5. **Facilitator prompts** - e.g. "What's the evidence that this is above the level expectation?", "Would we rate this the same if someone else delivered it?"
6. **Post-meeting checks** - distribution by manager and by demographic group (where lawful), documentation of rating changes and reasons.
7. **Template** for recording each change and its rationale.

Rules: only analyze demographic patterns where that data is lawfully collected, suppress any group under 5 people, and do not invent counts - work only from what I provide.
variables: counts by rating per manager - optional

title: Facilitate a risk and control self-assessment workshop
description: Plans a risk and control self-assessment session with business owners: agenda, prompts, a rating guide, and a capture template.
content:
Help me plan and run a risk and control self-assessment (RCSA) workshop.

**Business area:** [e.g. treasury operations, customer onboarding, claims]
**Participants:** [ROLES and how familiar they are with risk language]
**Existing risks and controls on record:** [PASTE or "starting from scratch"]
**Recent events:** [incidents, losses, audit findings, process or system changes]
**Our rating scales:** [impact and likelihood definitions, or "suggest one"]
**Time available:** [e.g. 2 hours]

Give me:
1. **Pre-work** for participants - a short email and 3 questions to think about beforehand.
2. **Agenda** with timings.
3. **Facilitation prompts** in everyday language for: identifying what could go wrong, how they would know, what stops it today, and what has nearly happened.
4. **Rating guide** - inherent risk, control effectiveness, residual risk - with concrete examples for this business area so ratings are consistent.
5. **Challenge questions** to test optimistic ratings, e.g. "When did this control last catch something?", "What happens when that person is on leave?", "How do you know the report is complete?"
6. **Capture template** - columns: Risk, Cause, Impact, Inherent rating, Controls, Control effectiveness, Residual rating, Action, Owner, Due date.
7. **Follow-up email** summarizing outcomes and actions.

Keep the tone collaborative: the goal is honest assessment, not a test participants pass or fail.
variables: e.g. treasury operations, customer onboarding, claims
ROLES and how familiar they are with risk language
incidents, losses, audit findings, process or system changes
impact and likelihood definitions, or "suggest one"

title: Find meeting times across time zones and write the invite
description: Workable meeting slots for attendees in several time zones, a fair rotation if it recurs, and a ready-to-send invitation.
content:
Help me schedule a meeting across time zones.

**Attendees and their locations/time zones:** [e.g. "my executive - New York; CFO - London; partner - Singapore"]
**Working hours or constraints for each:** [e.g. "no calls after 7pm local", "Fridays off in Dubai"]
**Meeting length and purpose:** [DETAILS]
**Date range:** [e.g. "next 2 weeks"]
**One-off or recurring?** [if recurring, how often]
**Whose time matters most:** [e.g. "external partner gets the best slot"]

Give me:
1. A table of the 3 best slots showing each attendee's local time and day, and who is outside normal hours.
2. If no slot works for everyone, say so and suggest options: split into two sessions, record and share, or rotate the inconvenient time.
3. For a recurring meeting, a fair rotation so the same people don't always take early or late calls.
4. Daylight-saving changes in the date range that will shift local times - flag them so I can double-check [CONFIRM DST DATES].
5. The calendar invite: title, agenda in 3 bullets, times written in each attendee's zone, and the video link placeholder [ADD LINK].
6. A short email proposing the options and asking people to confirm by [DATE].

Double-check the time conversions and show your working for the first slot so I can verify it.
variables: e.g. "no calls after 7pm local", "Fridays off in Dubai"
e.g. "external partner gets the best slot"

title: Find the hidden dynamics in a meeting transcript
description: Spots unspoken disagreements, concerns, and alignment gaps in a transcript.
content:
Act as an organizational dynamics analyst.

**Context**
The transcript contains both explicit statements and patterns that may reveal concerns, assumptions, priorities, or misalignment.

**Task**
Identify:
- Repeated concerns
- Hidden assumptions
- Conflicting priorities
- Unanswered questions
- Areas of alignment
- Areas of potential misalignment

Clearly label observations versus interpretations. Do not speculate about personal motives.

**Format**
Use:
| Theme | Evidence | Interpretation | Confidence | Follow-up |

**Transcript:** [PASTE]

title: Find unresolved issues in meeting notes and follow-up questions to close them
description: Lists every open loop a meeting left behind, why it is stuck, who should close it, and the exact follow-up questions to send.
content:
Review my meeting notes and find everything that was left unresolved, then give me the follow-up questions that will close each item.

**Meeting purpose:** [what the meeting was meant to settle]
**Notes or transcript:** [PASTE]
**People involved and their roles:** [NAMES AND ROLES]

Look for:
- Questions raised but not answered.
- Decisions deferred ("let's take this offline", "we'll come back to this").
- Actions with no owner or no date.
- Disagreements that ended without agreement.
- Assumptions or numbers people said they would check.
- Dependencies on people who were not in the room.

Return:
1. A table: | Unresolved issue | Why it is open (missing info / no owner / disagreement / waiting on someone) | Who can close it | Risk if left open (High/Med/Low) | Suggested deadline |
2. For each High and Medium item, 1-3 specific follow-up questions, written so I can paste them into an email or a Teams or Slack message. Address each question to the person who can answer it.
3. Items that should go on the next meeting's agenda vs. items that can be closed asynchronously.
4. Anything the notes are too thin to judge, so I can check with attendees.

Quote the notes briefly as evidence for each issue. Do not invent issues that are not supported by the notes, and do not guess at answers.
variables: what the meeting was meant to settle

title: Find where a meeting went off-topic and how to run it tighter
description: Shows where a meeting drifted off-topic, how much time it cost, and specific changes to keep the next one on track.
content:
Review this meeting transcript and show me where the discussion went off-topic and how to run the next one more tightly.

**Meeting purpose and agenda:** [PASTE]
**Planned length vs. actual length:** [e.g. "planned 30 min, ran 55 min"]
**Transcript (with timestamps if available):** [PASTE]

Analyze:
- Each stretch where the discussion left the agenda: what it was about, roughly how long it lasted (use timestamps if present; otherwise estimate and say so), and who it mattered to.
- Whether each tangent was useful (surfaced a real issue) or not.
- Patterns: agenda items with no clear outcome, problem-solving in a status meeting, the same point repeated, deep dives that needed only 2 people.

Return:
1. **Table:** | Off-topic discussion | Approx. time | Useful? (Yes / Partly / No) | Where it belongs instead (separate meeting, async thread, 1:1, parking lot) |
2. **Time summary:** share of the meeting spent on the agenda vs. off it.
3. **Useful tangents to follow up**, with a suggested owner.
4. **5 specific changes for next time**, such as a timeboxed agenda, a stated outcome per item, a parking lot, or a facilitator phrase to redirect politely.
5. **3 redirect phrases** I can use in the moment without sounding rude.

Describe topics and patterns, not individuals' behavior. Keep the tone constructive so I could share the findings with the group.

title: Fix a recurring meeting that wastes time
description: Diagnoses a recurring meeting and redesigns its purpose, format, attendees, and cadence — or recommends cancelling it.
content:
Act as a workplace productivity consultant specializing in meeting effectiveness.

**Context**
This recurring meeting consumes [TIME/FREQUENCY] and currently follows the format below.

**Task**
Determine what should be eliminated, shortened, delegated, standardized, automated, or moved asynchronous. Preserve the business outcome while reducing meeting time and cognitive load.

**Format**
Return:
| Current activity | Keep / Change / Remove | Better method | Expected benefit |
Then provide the redesigned meeting agenda.

**Current format:** [PASTE]

title: Generate sharp questions to ask in a meeting
description: Questions that surface assumptions, risks, and trade-offs others may miss.
content:
Act as a strategic facilitator skilled at uncovering assumptions, risks, trade-offs, and decisions.

**Context**
The meeting objective is [OBJECTIVE] and the participants are [PARTICIPANTS].

**Task**
Generate the questions most likely to improve the quality of the discussion. Prioritize questions that expose assumptions, clarify decision criteria, identify dependencies, surface risks, and move the group toward an actionable outcome. Avoid generic questions.

**Format**
Return the top 10 questions grouped into:
- Clarify
- Challenge
- Decide
- Commit

**Context:** [PASTE]

title: Map each stakeholder's needs, agreements, and conflicts from a meeting
description: Summarizes each person's needs and position from a discussion and shows the areas of alignment and conflict to work on.
content:
Analyze this discussion and show me what each stakeholder needs, where they agree, and where their views conflict.

**Topic of the discussion:** [WHAT WAS BEING DISCUSSED]
**Participants and roles:** [NAMES AND ROLES]
**Transcript, notes, or email/chat thread:** [PASTE]
**My role and goal:** [e.g. "I lead the project and need everyone aligned on scope"]

Return:
1. **Stakeholder table:** | Person/role | Stated position | Underlying need or concern | What they would accept | Evidence (short quote or paraphrase) |
2. **Areas of alignment:** points most or all stakeholders agree on, which I can build from.
3. **Areas of conflict:** each disagreement, who is on which side, and whether it is about facts, priorities, resources, or approach.
4. **Possible bridges:** for each conflict, 1-2 options that could meet both sides' underlying needs.
5. **Who to talk to next and what to ask,** in priority order.

Rules:
- Base everything on what people said or wrote. Label any inference as [INFERRED] and keep inferences modest.
- Do not speculate about personalities or motives; describe positions and interests only.
- If someone said little, note that their position is unclear rather than guessing.
variables: e.g. "I lead the project and need everyone aligned on scope"

title: Plan a big-room or PI planning event
description: An agenda, preparation checklist, and facilitation plan for a multi-team planning event that ends with committed objectives and a dependency board.
content:
Help me plan a big-room planning event (such as SAFe PI planning or a quarterly multi-team planning session).

**Teams attending:** [NUMBER of teams, roles, locations]
**Planning horizon:** [e.g. next 10-12 weeks / one quarter]
**Business priorities for the period:** [TOP features or objectives]
**Format and length:** [in person / remote / hybrid, 1 or 2 days]
**Tools:** [physical board, Miro, Jira, etc.]
**Problems from past planning sessions:** [e.g. "dependencies found too late", "overcommitment"]

Return:
1. **Preparation checklist** (2-4 weeks before): prioritized backlog ready, capacity per team calculated (holidays, support load, leave), architecture and dependency pre-work, logistics, and briefings for leaders.
2. **Agenda** with timings for each day: business context, product vision, team breakouts, draft plan review, management problem-solving, final plan review, risk review, and confidence vote.
3. **Team breakout guidance**: how to size work against capacity, leave a buffer (typically 15-20%), and write objectives in business terms.
4. **Dependency board**: how to capture and confirm cross-team dependencies, with a rule that every dependency needs both teams' agreement.
5. **Risk handling**: sort risks into resolved, owned, accepted, or mitigated.
6. **Confidence vote**: how to run it and what to do with low scores.
7. **Remote or hybrid adjustments**, if relevant.
8. **Outputs and follow-up**: what should be published within 48 hours.

Flag where my situation suggests a lighter-weight version would work better.
variables: in person / remote / hybrid, 1 or 2 days

title: Plan a client kickoff meeting that sets expectations from day one
description: An agenda, talking points, and a decision checklist for the first meeting of a client engagement or agency project.
content:
Help me plan the kickoff meeting for a new client engagement.

**Client and project:** [WHO and WHAT]
**Agreed scope and deliverables:** [SUMMARY or paste from the SOW]
**Attendees from both sides:** [NAMES or ROLES]
**Length and format:** [e.g. "90 minutes, video call"]
**Risks I already see:** [e.g. unclear decision-maker, tight deadline, a team that didn't want outside help]

Give me:
1. A timed agenda covering: introductions and roles, goals and what success looks like, scope recap (including what's out of scope), timeline and milestones, ways of working, risks, and next steps.
2. Questions to ask so the client defines success in measurable terms.
3. A ways-of-working checklist to agree in the room: single point of contact, who approves deliverables, feedback turnaround time, revision rounds, meeting cadence, communication channels, and how change requests work.
4. How to state the scope boundaries politely but clearly, in a sentence or two I can say aloud.
5. Talking points for each risk I listed.
6. A kickoff recap email template that documents every agreement made, for both sides to confirm in writing.

Keep it practical. If my scope summary is vague anywhere, flag it before the meeting.
variables: SUMMARY or paste from the SOW

title: Plan a productive parent-teacher conference about a struggling student
description: Prepares an agenda, evidence, talking points, and shared next steps for a hard conference with a family.
content:
Help me prepare for a parent-teacher conference about a student who is struggling.

**Student's grade:** [GRADE]
**Concern:** [academic, behavior, attendance, social; be specific]
**Evidence:** [e.g. grades, work samples, assessment scores, behavior log with dates]
**What I've already tried:** [STRATEGIES and results]
**Student strengths:** [AT LEAST 2]
**Family context I know:** [e.g. language spoken at home, past contact, work schedule]
**Others attending:** [e.g. counselor, interpreter, student]
**Time slot:** [MINUTES]

Build:
1. A short agenda that starts with strengths and asks the family what they see at home before I share concerns.
2. Opening words that set a partnership tone.
3. How to present the concern with 2-3 specific pieces of evidence, not labels.
4. Questions to ask the family (routines, what works at home, the student's view).
5. 2-3 next steps split into school actions, home actions, and student actions, with a check-in date.
6. How to respond if the family gets upset, disagrees, or asks about special education evaluation. Explain that a written request for evaluation must be passed on and that I should not discourage it.
7. A follow-up note I can send afterward summarizing what we agreed.

Keep language free of education jargon. If an interpreter is needed, keep sentences short and plan extra time.
variables: academic, behavior, attendance, social; be specific
e.g. language spoken at home, past contact, work schedule

title: Plan a project kickoff meeting and kickoff deck
description: An agenda, slide-by-slide deck outline, and pre-work for a kickoff that aligns the team on goals, roles, and ways of working.
content:
Help me plan a project kickoff meeting and the deck for it.

**Project:** [NAME, goal, and why it matters now]
**Attendees:** [team members, sponsor, key stakeholders, vendors]
**Format and length:** [in person / remote, e.g. 90 minutes]
**What is already decided:** [scope, budget, dates, tools]
**What is still open:** [decisions or unknowns the team should help shape]
**My biggest worry going in:** [e.g. "two teams who have clashed before", "unclear sponsor"]

The kickoff must leave everyone able to answer: why are we doing this, what does done look like, who does what, how will we work together, and what happens next.

Return:
1. **Pre-work** - what to send 2-3 days before (e.g. charter, questions to think about).
2. **Agenda** with timings, owner per item, and the purpose of each block.
3. **Deck outline** - 8-12 slides, each with a title and 2-3 bullet points: sponsor's why, objectives and success measures, scope in/out, milestones, team and roles, ways of working (meetings, tools, decision rights, escalation path), top risks, next 2 weeks.
4. **One interactive exercise** that surfaces concerns early (e.g. a quick risk brainstorm or "what would make this fail").
5. **Opening remarks** for the sponsor (under 150 words).
6. **Follow-up email** template with decisions, actions, and owners.

Use [ADD] for any detail I have not given rather than making it up.
variables: NAME, goal, and why it matters now
team members, sponsor, key stakeholders, vendors
decisions or unknowns the team should help shape
e.g. "two teams who have clashed before", "unclear sponsor"

title: Plan a sales kickoff that changes how the team sells
description: A sales kickoff agenda built around a few behavior changes, with sessions, practice, and follow-through after the event.
content:
Help me plan a sales kickoff (SKO).

**Audience and size:** [roles, number of people, in person or virtual]
**Length:** [e.g. 1 day, 2 days]
**Last year's results and this year's target:** [HEADLINE NUMBERS]
**Strategic priorities for the year:** [e.g. new product, move upmarket, new pricing, new territory model]
**Skill gaps we see:** [e.g. discovery, multi-threading, negotiation]
**Budget and constraints:** [DETAILS]
**Speakers available:** [executives, customers, partners, product]

Design the SKO around 3 behavior changes, not a list of topics:
1. Name the 3 behaviors we want reps doing differently by the end of Q1.
2. Build the agenda backward from those: each block either explains why, shows how, or has reps practice.
3. Keep no more than 40% of time on presentations; the rest is practice, role-play, and peer learning.
4. Include recognition moments, a customer voice, and time for regional or team breakouts.
5. Plan the follow-through: the 30/60/90-day reinforcement, manager coaching guides, and how we measure adoption.

Return:
- The 3 target behaviors and how we'll measure each.
- A timed agenda: Time | Session | Format | Owner | Outcome.
- A brief for each speaker (what to cover, what to avoid, length).
- A post-event survey and reinforcement plan.
- Logistics checklist.

Use only the figures and speakers I provide; mark anything missing as [ADD].
variables: roles, number of people, in person or virtual

title: Plan and facilitate a kaizen improvement workshop
description: A plan for a focused 1-5 day improvement event, from scoping and team selection to daily agenda and follow-up.
content:
Help me plan a kaizen (rapid improvement) workshop.

**Process to improve:** [e.g. "inbound receiving", "invoice approval", "changeover on line 3"]
**The problem and current performance:** [e.g. "receiving takes 6 hours per truck, target is 3"]
**Target:** [MEASURABLE GOAL]
**Duration available:** [e.g. "3 days", "two half-days"]
**People available:** [ROLES - include those who do the work]
**Limits:** [budget, can't stop production, approvals needed]

Give me:
1. A one-page charter: scope (start and end of process), what's out of scope, goal, team, sponsor, and date of report-out.
2. Pre-work for the 2 weeks before: data to collect, observations to make, people to tell.
3. A detailed agenda for each day: understand current state (go see, map the process, measure), find waste and root causes, generate and test ideas, implement, standardize, report out.
4. Facilitation tips: how to get frontline people talking, avoid jumping to solutions, and handle a manager who dominates.
5. A 30-day follow-up list template: action | owner | date | status, and how to sustain the gains.
6. A report-out structure for leadership (before/after, results, open actions).

Keep the goal realistic for the time we have; tell me if my scope is too big.
variables: e.g. "receiving takes 6 hours per truck, target is 3"
ROLES - include those who do the work
budget, can't stop production, approvals needed

title: Plan the board pack timeline and chase contributors
description: A backward-planned schedule for assembling the board pack, with owners, deadlines, and reminder messages that keep it on time.
content:
Help me plan and run the board pack process for an upcoming meeting.

**Meeting date:** [DATE]
**Pack distribution deadline:** [e.g. "7 days before"]
**Agenda items and paper owners:** [LIST - item, owner, type of paper]
**Approvals needed before release:** [e.g. "CEO review, CFO sign-off, legal review"]
**Format and platform:** [e.g. "single PDF via board portal"]
**What went wrong last time:** [e.g. "finance papers arrived the night before"]

Give me:
1. **Backward timeline:** table - date | milestone | owner (first drafts due, review rounds, final papers, compilation, CEO review, distribution). Build in a buffer before the distribution deadline.
2. **Paper standards to send contributors:** cover sheet fields (purpose, decision required, key points, risks), page limits, file naming, template.
3. **Tracker:** paper | owner | draft due | received | reviewed | final | notes.
4. **Reminder messages:** a kickoff email, a friendly reminder 3 days before the draft deadline, a firm one on the day, and an escalation note to my executive for anything overdue - polite and clear about the knock-on effect.
5. **Compilation checklist:** page numbers, index, version control, consistent formatting, confidentiality markings, broken links, and final read-through.

Keep the messages short and specific about what's due and when.
variables: LIST - item, owner, type of paper
e.g. "CEO review, CFO sign-off, legal review"
e.g. "finance papers arrived the night before"

title: Prepare a monthly S&OP meeting pack and decision agenda
description: A sales and operations planning pack that reconciles demand, supply, and inventory and frames the decisions leaders must make.
content:
Help me prepare the pack for our monthly sales and operations planning (S&OP) meeting.

**Planning horizon and product families:** [e.g. "18 months, 6 product families"]
**Demand plan vs. last month and vs. actuals:** [PASTE OR SUMMARIZE BY FAMILY]
**Forecast accuracy and bias:** [e.g. MAPE, bias by family]
**Supply plan and constraints:** [CAPACITY, SUPPLIER LIMITS, LEAD TIMES, LABOR]
**Inventory position vs. target:** [DAYS OF SUPPLY OR UNITS BY FAMILY]
**Financial plan to reconcile against:** [REVENUE OR VOLUME TARGETS]
**Known events:** [PROMOTIONS, LAUNCHES, PRICE CHANGES, SUPPLIER ISSUES]
**Attendees:** [WHO DECIDES]

Build the pack to follow the S&OP flow: demand review, supply review, gap reconciliation, executive decisions.

For each product family, show demand vs. supply vs. inventory target and flag gaps (shortfall or excess) with the volume and revenue at stake.

For every material gap, frame a decision with 2-3 options (e.g. add overtime, reallocate supply, push a promotion back, build inventory ahead), the trade-off of each, and who owns it.

Use only the figures I give; label missing data [ADD DATA]. Do not reconcile numbers by guessing.

Return:
1. A one-page executive summary: top 3 risks, top 3 decisions needed.
2. A table by family: Demand | Supply | Gap | Inventory vs. target | Revenue at risk | Proposed action.
3. A 60-minute agenda with time boxes.
4. A decision log template for the meeting.
variables: CAPACITY, SUPPLIER LIMITS, LEAD TIMES, LABOR
DAYS OF SUPPLY OR UNITS BY FAMILY
PROMOTIONS, LAUNCHES, PRICE CHANGES, SUPPLIER ISSUES

title: Prepare for a first meeting with a new business leader I support

Give me:

title: Prepare for a parent-teacher conference
description: A one-page plan with priorities, questions, and notes to bring so a short conference turns into real next steps.
content:
Help me prepare for a parent-teacher conference.

**Child's grade and subjects:** [DETAILS]
**Length of the conference:** [e.g. "15 minutes"]
**What I know from report cards, apps, or homework:** [GRADES, COMMENTS, PATTERNS]
**What my child says about school:** [THEIR VIEW]
**What I'm proud of:** [STRENGTHS]
**What worries me:** [CONCERNS]
**Anything the school should know:** [e.g. "new sibling", "diagnosis", "move", "illness"]

Give me:
1. My top 2-3 goals for the conference, in priority order, so the time isn't eaten by small things.
2. 8-10 questions to ask, grouped by: progress, behavior and friendships, how to help at home. Mark the ones to ask first.
3. A short opening (2-3 sentences) that sets a teamwork tone.
4. How to respond if I hear something unexpected or upsetting, without getting defensive.
5. A note-taking template: what was said, agreed actions (who does what by when), follow-up date.
6. A short thank-you and follow-up email to send afterward, with blanks for the agreed actions.

If my concerns suggest a possible learning difference or need for extra support, list what I can ask the school about (such as an evaluation) and suggest I confirm the process with the school, since it varies by district.

title: Prepare for a productive meeting with my research advisor
description: Creates a focused agenda and progress update so advisor meetings end with decisions, feedback, and clear next steps.
content:
Help me prepare for my next meeting with my research advisor or supervisor.

**Meeting length and how often we meet:** [e.g. "30 minutes, every 2 weeks"]
**Progress since last meeting:** [what I did, results, drafts]
**What I'm stuck on:** [technical, conceptual, writing, motivation]
**Decisions I need from them:** [e.g. "which analysis to prioritize", "whether to submit to conference X"]
**Last meeting's action items:** [LIST and status]
**Anything delicate:** [e.g. "I'm behind schedule", "authorship question", "workload", "considering a different direction"]

Create:
1. A one-paragraph update I can send 24 hours ahead, so the meeting starts with discussion rather than catching up.
2. An agenda ordered by importance, with time per item, putting decisions first.
3. For each stuck point: a short framing of the problem, what I tried, and 2 options I'm considering, so I'm asking for a judgment, not a rescue.
4. Phrasing for any delicate topic that is honest and solution-focused.
5. A template for notes and a follow-up email that confirms decisions and action items with dates.

Keep everything brief; my advisor's time is limited.

title: Prepare for a tough conversation with an unhappy key account
description: A meeting plan for facing a frustrated customer executive: what to say, what to own, and how to agree a recovery plan.
content:
I have a meeting with an unhappy key customer. Help me prepare.

**Account and stakes:** [CONTRACT VALUE, RENEWAL DATE, STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE]
**Who I'm meeting:** [ROLES, their mood, what they've said in writing]
**What went wrong:** [TIMELINE OF ISSUES, our mistakes, their part if any]
**What's been fixed and what hasn't:** [DETAILS]
**What I can offer:** [e.g. dedicated support, roadmap commitment, credits, exec involvement - only approved items]
**Who's joining from my side:** [NAMES/ROLES]

Give me:
1. Their likely goals and fears for this meeting, and what a good outcome looks like for both sides.
2. An agenda (30-45 minutes) that lets them speak first.
3. Opening words: acknowledge the impact specifically, take ownership of our part, no excuses or over-promising.
4. Questions to understand what would restore their confidence.
5. Hard questions they may ask ("Why should we renew?", "Who's accountable?", "What's different this time?") with honest answers.
6. A recovery plan outline to agree in the room: actions, owners, dates, and how we'll report progress.
7. Roles for my colleagues in the meeting, and a follow-up email draft.

Do not suggest commitments or concessions I haven't listed as approved. If something requires approval, mark it [GET APPROVAL].
variables: CONTRACT VALUE, RENEWAL DATE, STRATEGIC IMPORTANCE
ROLES, their mood, what they've said in writing
TIMELINE OF ISSUES, our mistakes, their part if any

Act as a strategic meeting preparation advisor.

I have an upcoming meeting about the topic below. I want to enter the meeting prepared for the business issue, stakeholder dynamics, likely questions, and decisions.

- **What I need to know**

title: Prepare to discuss a tough audit finding with management
description: Prepares me for a closing meeting or difficult conversation about a finding, with key messages, likely pushback, and responses.
content:
Help me prepare for a meeting where I will present a difficult audit or compliance finding to management.

**The finding:** [CONDITION, cause, effect, proposed rating]
**Evidence:** [what supports it]
**Who will be in the room:** [ROLES and what they care about]
**Pushback I expect:** [e.g. "it's a one-off", "the rating is too harsh", "we don't have resources", "this isn't our responsibility"]
**What I need from the meeting:** [agreement on facts, agreed rating, owner and date for actions]
**Meeting length:** [e.g. 45 minutes]
**Relationship context:** [e.g. first audit of this area, history of tension, new leader]

Give me:
1. **Meeting structure** - opening, facts, impact, discussion, agreement on next steps; with timings that fit the meeting length.
2. **Key messages** - three sentences I must land, in plain business language.
3. **Pushback map** - table: Likely objection, What may be valid in it, My response, Evidence to point to.
4. **Where I can flex and where I cannot** - e.g. wording and action timelines can be negotiated; facts and independence cannot.
5. **Questions to ask** that move from defending to solving, e.g. "What would make this control workable for your team?"
6. **If we do not agree** - how to record management's disagreement and escalate appropriately.
7. **Follow-up email** summarizing what was agreed.

Tone: firm on facts, collaborative on solutions, respectful of management's perspective. Never change a rating just to keep the peace; change it only for new evidence.

title: Pull the decisions out of a meeting transcript

Act as a meeting governance analyst who distinguishes decisions from discussion.

**Context**
I need a reliable record of what was actually decided during the meeting.

**Task**
Review the transcript and identify every explicit decision, agreement, disagreement, and unresolved decision. Quote only short supporting phrases where needed. Do not treat a suggestion or opinion as a final decision.

**Format**
Use:
| Topic | Type | Decision/Position | Evidence | Owner/Next Step |

Types: Decision, Agreement, Disagreement, Unresolved.

title: Replace a meeting with an async update in email, Teams, or Slack
description: Turns what would have been a meeting into a clear written update that gets the needed input and decisions without a call.
content:
Turn this meeting into an async update so we can skip the call.

**What the meeting was going to cover:** [AGENDA OR TOPICS]
**Updates and information to share:** [PASTE NOTES, STATUS, DATA]
**Input or decisions I need from people:** [WHAT I NEED AND FROM WHOM]
**Where it will be posted:** [email / Teams or Slack channel / shared doc]
**Response deadline:** [DATE AND TIME]

Write the update so that:
- The first 2 lines say why there is no meeting and what I need from readers, by when.
- Information-only items are short bullets that need no reply.
- Each item that needs input is numbered, names who should respond, and asks a specific question (a choice between options, a yes/no, or a number), not "thoughts?".
- Context needed to answer is included or linked, so nobody has to ask.
- It ends with what happens if no one objects by the deadline (e.g. "we proceed with option A").

Return:
1. The async update, formatted for the channel I chose (subject line if email; short sections if Teams or Slack).
2. A short reminder message for the day before the deadline.
3. A note on what would justify calling a short meeting after all (e.g. strong disagreement on item 2).

Use only the facts I provided; mark anything missing as [ADD].

title: Run a 15-minute daily operations huddle that solves problems
description: An agenda, metrics board layout, and facilitation script for a short daily huddle that surfaces issues and assigns owners.

Design a daily operations huddle (stand-up) for my team.

**What goes wrong with our current huddle (if any):** [e.g. "turns into a status monologue", "runs 40 minutes", "same issues every day"]

Give me:

2. A board or slide layout: what columns and metrics to show, and how to mark red/green against target.
3. Rules for the huddle: what belongs there vs. what gets taken offline, how to stop problem-solving in the room, and who speaks when.
4. An action log format: issue | owner | due date | status, and how to review it daily so actions don't go stale.
5. A short script I can use to open the huddle and to cut off a discussion politely.
6. How to escalate problems the team can't solve to the next level (and how to report back).

Keep it practical for a frontline team; no jargon unless I've used it.

title: Run a deal-by-deal pipeline review with a sales rep
description: A focused pipeline review agenda with the right questions per stage, so the meeting coaches deals instead of just reading CRM.

Help me prepare a pipeline review meeting with one of my reps.

**Rep and segment:** [DETAILS]
**Meeting length:** [e.g. 45 minutes]
**Rep's quota, closed to date, and forecast call:** [NUMBERS]
**Open pipeline:** [paste deals: account, amount, stage, close date, next step, last activity date, days in stage]
**Our stage definitions or exit criteria:** [paste, or "use common B2B stages"]
**What I'm worried about:** [e.g. coverage, slipping dates, stale deals, one big deal]

Prepare:
1. A triage of the pipeline: which deals to discuss (largest, closing this period, stuck longest, missing next steps) and which to skip.
2. For each selected deal, 2-3 questions matched to its stage. Early-stage: is the pain real and quantified? Late-stage: who signs, what's the paper process, what could stop it? Avoid yes/no questions.
3. Hygiene issues to fix after the meeting: past close dates, no next step, stage that doesn't match evidence.
4. A coverage check: pipeline for this period and next vs what the rep needs.

Return:
- A timed agenda.
- A table: Deal | Why discuss | Questions | What a good answer sounds like.
- A hygiene list for the rep to clean up, with a deadline.
- A short follow-up note template summarizing agreed actions and dates.

Keep it coaching, not interrogation: the goal is better deals and a more accurate forecast. Use only the deal data I provide; mark missing fields [CONFIRM] rather than guessing.

title: Run a pre-shift lineup meeting for restaurant or hotel staff

Write a pre-shift lineup briefing for me to deliver.

title: Run a prioritization workshop with stakeholders
description: A facilitation plan that gets competing stakeholders to agree on priorities using shared criteria.
content:
Help me plan and facilitate a prioritization workshop with stakeholders who want different things.

**Participants:** [ROLES AND WHAT EACH IS PUSHING FOR]
**Items to prioritize:** [LIST, OR ROUGH COUNT]
**Goal or strategy we are prioritizing against:** [OKRS, THEMES]
**Capacity available:** [e.g. one team for a quarter]
**Time:** [e.g. 90 minutes, in person or remote]
**Known tensions:** [CONFLICTS, POLITICS]

Design the session:
1. Pre-work: what to send and ask for beforehand, including evidence for each item.
2. Criteria: propose 3-5 scoring criteria tied to the goal (e.g. customer impact, strategic fit, confidence, effort) and how to agree on them at the start, before anyone sees scores.
3. Method: pick the best fit for this group, e.g. scoring matrix, buy-a-feature with a fixed budget, or forced ranking, and explain why.

5. How to handle deadlocks: tie-breakers and who has final say.
6. Output: what the group leaves with and how decisions get recorded.
7. A follow-up message template summarizing the decisions, what did not make the cut, and why.

Keep it practical; I will run it myself.
